title: What psychologists say about boredom: an unpleasant signal that may help creative thinking

sources.title: Attentional states and creative potential (2022; summarizes Mann & Cadman, 2014)
Does Being Bored Make Us More Creative? (Mann & Cadman, Creativity Research Journal, 2014)
sources.license: repository record; only facts are used

sources.title: People are increasingly bored in our digital age (Tam & Inzlicht, 2024)

facts.text: Psychologists define boredom as the unpleasant state of wanting, but being unable, to engage in a satisfying activity.
Some scientists see boredom as a signal, like an alarm, that it is time to move on to something different.
When people cannot escape a dull situation, their minds tend to wander, and boredom may lead to more ideas and creativity.
In experiments by Mann and Cadman, people who first did a boring task gave more creative answers than a control group that did not.
Researchers argue that turning to digital media is a poor way to cope with boredom and may leave people more bored.

notes: 混合題 mixed-top-01 用（2026-10-09 線上查證，只取事實、不取原句）。Mann & Cadman 的效果在後續研究中不一定重現，選文只寫「在一個知名實驗中」，並用 may、suspect 等字保留語氣；第二篇是虛構的學生經驗文，不含事實主張。
